opportunities.finding: The LLM adapter is the single highest-leverage unblock. runtime-deps.ts:5 returns the prompt back, so 100% of insight.generated and tweet.drafted events in the last 2h are literal '[mock-llm] Write one concise tweet about: ...' echoes. Wiring one real model call converts every downstream metric from noise into signal and is a one-file change.

The publish funnel is structurally impossible today: social.postTweet (runtime-deps.ts:11) returns mock_<ts> and posts nowhere, ops_social_posts has 0 rows and tweet.posted has 0 lifetime rows, while 68 drafts were produced today and the 8/day quota is untouched. The cheapest genuine growth datapoint in the org is one real post - and it cannot exist until the poster is real.

Queue relief is real but not durable. Queued fell 152 -> 62 and p50 wait 238min -> 95min, yet that came entirely from one burst hour (16:00Z, 173 steps succeeded, 19 tweet drafts, 13 content drafts, 6 step.recovered). Steady-state drain since then is 3-8 steps/h against 12-21 arrivals/h, so the backlog rebuilds at roughly +10/h and p50 wait exceeds 100min again within a day.

Draft diversity is zero even before mockness: all 25 sampled tweet drafts in 12h carry the identical topic string 'high-signal company update for audience engagement'. Even a real LLM over a single frozen topic produces one recycled post - topic entropy has to enter the pipeline before draft volume means anything.

Policy is decorative. content_policy.max_drafts_per_day=8 was exceeded 8.5x today (68 drafts) and auto_approve.allowed_step_kinds is never read. Only x_daily_quota is consulted, and only for post_tweet steps - which never occur - so no effective governance exists over a loop that auto-accepted 149/150 proposals in 6h with zero approval events logged.

risks.risk: Critical: publishing is unsafe in the current state. Enabling the post path before the LLM is real would push prompt echoes to a live audience (draft bodies currently contain the literal string '[mock-llm] Write one concise tweet about: ...'). Fix order matters: real model first, real poster second.

High: the mock/real conclusion in the previous cycle was a measurement artifact and must be corrected. That cycle read '52% non-mock, real LLM partially live' by sampling the payload field of mixed-kind events; a payload-only check on proposal.created rows (no mock text) inflates the real share. Measured on the artifact payloads themselves, mock rate is 100% and there is no real LLM path at all. Any dashboard built on the 52% number is wrong.

High: missions never terminate. 65 missions created in 3h, 0 finished, status stuck at 'approved' even when every step succeeded. Mission-level metrics (completion rate, cycle latency, per-mission outcome) are permanently unmeasurable, and no failed-mission alarm can ever fire because the failure is recorded on the step, not the mission.

High: uncontrolled autonomy. isAutoApproveAllowed() returns true unconditionally and the only gate is the x_daily_quota check for post_tweet. With 149/150 auto-accepted and 0 proposal.approved/rejected events logged, there is no audit trail of why anything was accepted - and no lever to stop the loop if it starts writing to a live channel.

Medium: step-kind validation is missing at creation time, so prose gets used as a kind and dead-letters at execution ('Unknown step kind: priority balancing and blocker removal', 'coordinate', 'get'). 51 steps have dead-lettered this way; the failure mode is discovered only after queueing and a claim.

Medium: the hour-16 burst produced 19 tweet drafts in 60 minutes. Once posting works, an unthrottled burst plus an unenforced daily draft limit of 8 could publish 8 near-identical posts in one day to a live audience - the reputational version of R1, arriving in a batch.

decision: Stop optimizing analysis volume - 8 insights/h is not the constraint. The constraint is that the entire pipeline is wired to a prompt-echo LLM and a no-op poster, so 100% of content is synthetic and 0 rows ever land in the publish funnel. Ship E1 (real model) first and E2 (one real post) second; E3-E6 are one-hour hygiene that make the first live post safe. Also correct last cycle's 52%-real claim: it was a sampling artifact, the mock rate is 100%.
diffFromPrevCycle: Queue improved sharply but from one burst hour only: queued 152 -> 62, p50 wait 238min -> 95min, p90 432 -> 138min, stale running steps 6 -> 1 (one analyze step still frozen since 08:46Z).
Arrival still exceeds steady-state drain (12-21/h vs 3-8/h), so the backlog rebuilds unless E3 lands.

Missions: 65 created in 3h, 0 finished (was 59/0) - missions still never reach a terminal state.
Funnel unchanged at zero: tweet.posted lifetime 0, ops_social_posts rows 0, but drafts today rose to 37 tweet + 31 content against an unenforced 8/day policy cap.
